grammar.title: Going to
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Going to** é a forma mais comum de falar de **planos e intenções** — coisas que você **já decidiu** fazer.

**Estrutura:** sujeito + **am/is/are** + **going to** + verbo base
- I**'m going to** travel to Chile in July.
- She**'s not going to** buy a car.
- **Are** you **going to** study tonight?

Também usamos para **previsões com evidência** (algo que você vê que vai acontecer):
- "Look at those clouds! It**'s going to** rain."
- "Be careful! You**'re going to** fall!"

**Gonna:** na fala informal, "going to" vira **gonna**: "I'm **gonna** call you." Você vai ouvir muito em séries e músicas. Use na fala, evite na escrita formal.

Com **go**, é comum simplificar: "I'm going to go to the beach" → "I'm **going to the beach**."

rows: What are you going to do?

examples.en: We're going to book the hotel tonight.
examples.pt: Vamos reservar o hotel hoje à noite.

examples.en: I'm going to save money for a backpacking trip.
Oh no, the phone is at 1%. It's going to die!
examples.pt: Ah não, o celular está com 1%. Vai desligar!

grammar.tip_pt: Não esqueça o **to be**: "I going to..." ❌ → "I**'m** going to..." ✅. É a mesma "cola" do present continuous.

common_mistakes.why_pt: Going to precisa do verbo to be.
Depois de going to, use o verbo na forma base.

common_mistakes.wrong: I will to visit my mom.
common_mistakes.right: I'm going to visit my mom. / I will visit my mom.

pronunciation.tip_pt: **Going to** + verbo vira **gonna** ("gâna") na fala: "I'm gonna go" = "áim gâna gôu". Atenção: só vira gonna quando é futuro. "I'm going **to** the gym" (estou indo para) **não** vira "gonna the gym"!

grammar.title: Present continuous para o futuro
grammar.explanation_pt:
Surpresa: o **present continuous** também fala do **futuro**! Usamos para **compromissos já combinados** — com hora, lugar ou outra pessoa envolvida (o que está "na agenda").

- "I**'m seeing** the dentist tomorrow at 10."
- "We**'re having** dinner with Ana on Friday."
- "What **are** you **doing** this weekend?"

É obrigatório ter uma **expressão de futuro** (tomorrow, on Friday, next week) ou o contexto deixar claro.

**Going to x present continuous:**
- **going to** = intenção, plano na cabeça: "I'm going to call the dentist." (pretendo ligar)
- **present continuous** = já está marcado: "I'm seeing the dentist on Monday." (consulta marcada)

Na prática, os dois muitas vezes funcionam. Mas para perguntar a agenda de alguém, o natural é: **"What are you doing on Saturday?"**

grammar.tip_pt: Para horários **oficiais** (trens, voos, aulas, filmes), use o **simple present**: "The train **leaves** at 8:15." / "The movie **starts** at 9."

common_mistakes.why_pt: Para perguntar planos, use o present continuous.

grammar.title: Convites e sugestões
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Convidar:**
- **Would you like to** + verbo? (educado, neutro) → "Would you like to come to dinner?"
- **Do you want to** + verbo? (informal, entre amigos) → "Do you wanna watch a movie?"

**Would like x like:**
- **like** = gostar (em geral): "I **like** coffee."
- **would like** = gostaria/quero (agora, educado): "I**'d like** a coffee, please."

**Sugerir:**
- **Let's** + verbo → "**Let's** order pizza!"
- **How about / What about** + verbo-**ing** → "**How about going** to the movies?"
- **Why don't we** + verbo? → "**Why don't we** try the new restaurant?"

**Responder:**
✅ Aceitar: "I'd love to!" / "Sounds great!" / "Count me in!" / "Sure, why not?"
❌ Recusar com educação: **agradecer + desculpa + motivo + (alternativa)**:
"**Thanks** for the invite! **I'm afraid I can't** — **I'm working** that night. **Maybe another time?**"

reading.title: The art of saying no
reading.text: Many people find it hard to say no to invitations. They're afraid of being rude. But experts say that a polite "no" is better than a "yes" you regret. Here's a simple formula: 1. Thank the person: "Thanks so much for inviting me!" 2. Say no clearly: "I'm afraid I can't make it." 3. Give a short reason (optional): "I need a quiet weekend." 4. Offer an alternative if you want: "How about coffee next week?" And remember: "Maybe" is not a polite answer if you mean "no" — it only creates expectations!

questions.answer: Thank the person.

questions.q: Is the reason obligatory?
questions.answer: No, it's optional.

questions.q: Why is "maybe" not a good answer?
questions.answer: It only creates expectations (if you mean no).

grammar.title: Will (e comparação com going to)
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Estrutura:** **will** + verbo base (igual para todas as pessoas, sem -s, sem to)
- Afirmativa: I**'ll** help. · Negativa: I **won't** (= will not) forget. · Pergunta: **Will** you be there?

**Usos de will:**
1. **Decisão na hora** (não planejada): "The phone is ringing!" → "I**'ll** get it!"
2. **Ofertas:** "Your bag looks heavy. I**'ll** carry it."
3. **Promessas:** "I **won't** be late, I promise."
4. **Pedidos em restaurante:** "I**'ll** have the fish."
5. **Previsões/opiniões** (sem evidência concreta): "I **think** robots **will** do most jobs." / "She**'ll probably** love it."

**Will x going to:**
- **going to** = já decidido antes: "I**'m going to** buy a car. I saved money for a year."
- **will** = decidido agora: "Oh, this car is on sale? OK, I**'ll** buy it!"

**Shall I...?** = Quer que eu...? (oferta, mais britânico): "**Shall I** call a taxi?"

grammar.tip_pt: **Won't** (will not) soa "uônt" — diferente de **want** ("uónt", querer). "I won't go" = não vou · "I want to go" = quero ir. Cuidado!

common_mistakes.wrong: "The phone is ringing!" "I'm going to answer it."

pronunciation.tip_pt: A contração **'ll** é um L escuro rápido, quase só a língua no céu da boca: **I'll** = "áil", **you'll** = "iúl", **it'll** = "íról". E **won't** ("uônt", com o "ô" fechado) ≠ **want** ("uónt").
practice: I won't forget. / I want to go.

reading.title: Predictions from the past
reading.text: In 1900, an American engineer made predictions for the year 2000. Some were right: "People will talk to friends in other countries by telephone," and "Photos will arrive from far away in seconds." Others were wrong: "There will be no letters C, X or Q in the alphabet," and "Mosquitoes and flies will disappear." Today, experts make new predictions: we'll live longer, cities will be greener, and AI will be part of everything. Will they be right? We'll see!
